children: OPEC must appreciate Iraq’s request for a higher oil output quota to offset its losses due to conflicts over the past four decades, the Arab country’s oil minister said.

Bassim Khudair said in a local TV interview that Iraq, OPEC’s second largest crude exporter, has been locked in talks with the group for an increase in its production quota, which is currently around 4.3 million barrels per day (bpd).
Khudair said Iraq has suffered from large losses over the past 40 years due to internal conflicts, external wars and military attacks by the ISIS (Daesh) militants.

“We are in a dialogue with OPEC about our position regarding an increase in our production quota…OPEC must understand Iraq’s position because Iraq is not like other OPEC members,” Khudair told Iraq’s Alikhbariya TV news channel.

“Iraq has been severely harmed for more than 40 years due to conflicts and wrong policies…Iraq suffered more due to Daesh attacks, and it defended the entire world by confronting Daesh…they must appreciate our request for more oil exports.”
In September last year, then prime minister Mohammed Al-Sudani used an international energy forum in Baghdad to demand a higher OPEC quota.

Al-Sudani justified the demand to what he described as Iraq’s enormous crude resources, large population, its growing oil production capacity and the need for more petrodollars to fund post-war development.
In June, the oil ministry rejected reports of Baghdad’s plans to withdraw from OPEC, instead calling for the reassessment of production quotas in line with the circumstances of member states.
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)
